idiom_name: make(chan T, n) with select { case ch <- v: default: }
implementation_notes: Go builds the pattern into the language: make(chan T, n) is a bounded FIFO whose capacity is fixed at creation, and the full-behaviour is expressed by how the send is written. A bare send blocks (back-pressure), select with a default case refuses the item, and select with ctx.Done() or a timer bounds the wait; drop-oldest or coalescing is a consumer-side concern, done by keeping only the newest value or draining a channel down to capacity. Effective Go's guidance that the buffer capacity limits the number of simultaneous calls is the sizing rule: pick n from the acceptable in-flight work, not from the heap. golang.org/x/sync/semaphore.Weighted is the alternative when the bound belongs to concurrency rather than to queued items.
code_sketch:
ch := make(chan Task, 1024)            // capacity fixed at creation
select {
case ch <- t:                          // admitted
case <-ctx.Done():                     // bounded wait: give up instead of blocking forever
default:                               // full: the decided outcome, visible at the send
    atomic.AddUint64(&dropped, 1)
}
pitfalls: len(ch) < cap(ch) does not make a send safe: the check and the send are not atomic, so another goroutine can take the slot - use select with default.
Sending on a closed channel panics and receiving from it yields zero values forever: shutdown needs exactly one closer plus a drain, otherwise the bound becomes a panic.
Blocking sends without a ctx.Done()/timer case turn a stalled consumer into leaked goroutines or a fleet-wide stall.
